key_insight: DLite shows that speculative decoding for agentic AI can be made history-free, avoiding the performance drop caused by carrying long KV cache histories across multi-turn interactions. The key breakthrough is a draft strategy that stays effective even as contexts grow and change continuously.
problem_solved: Existing speculative decoding draft models degrade badly in agentic workloads with long, evolving contexts and frequent back-and-forth turns. This leads to much lower acceptance rates and reduced speedup, even when historical KV cache is retained.
method: Uses a history-free speculative decoding design instead of relying on accumulated past KV cache.
Adapts draft token generation to agentic, multi-turn workloads where context changes continuously.
Improves acceptance length and decoding efficiency by reducing the mismatch between draft and target model behavior over long interactions.
impact: This matters because agentic AI systems need fast inference under long-context, interactive workloads where standard speculative decoding breaks down. DLite helps preserve speed gains in realistic deployment settings, making LLM agents more practical and efficient.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram comparing standard speculative decoding vs. DLite

Icon-based illustration of long multi-turn agent conversations and growing context
paper_title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
paper_authors: Jiaming Xu, Hanzhen Wang, Tianlang Zhao, Jiewen Xiao, Chengze Yuan
